output.reason: A diabetic patient with a 4-day-old plantar foot wound now showing surrounding redness, swelling and tenderness needs hands-on wound inspection, depth/probe assessment and same-day treatment decisions that messaging cannot provide.
output.patientMessage: Please be seen in person today — urgent care, your diabetes/foot clinic, or an emergency department if nothing else is open. A red, swollen, tender wound on a diabetic foot needs hands-on examination of the wound depth and same-day treatment. Keep weight off that foot. Go now, or sooner, if you develop fever, chills, spreading redness, streaking, drainage, black skin or foul smell.
differential: Diabetic foot wound infection with surrounding cellulitis
Deeper soft-tissue or bone involvement / abscess under the plantar wound

redFlags.concern: Spreading erythema and swelling around foot wound
redFlags.quote: the skin around it is red and a little swollen
tender when I press on it

redFlags.concern: Purulent drainage, black tissue or foul odor

output.vitalSigns: No vital sign values reported; the patient states "No fever" but whether a temperature was measured and by what method is unknown.
output.evidenceLimitations: Only consumer health summaries and an ED reference synthesis are available; neither establishes telehealth routing for this individual.

citations.claim: Consumer diabetes guidance advises prompt clinician evaluation for red, warm or painful skin on the feet.
citations.limitation: Consumer summary; does not specify setting, timing interval or treatment.

citations.claim: Serious diabetic foot problems can develop quickly, supporting a today rather than deferred assessment.
citations.limitation: General statement, not an individualized urgency threshold.
